REWARD_MACHINE:
STATES: u0, u1, u2, u3
INITIAL_STATE: u0
FINAL_STATES: u3
TRANSITION_FUNCTION:
(u0, has_door_key) -> u1
(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, door_open) -> u2
(u1, key_lost) -> u1
(u1, else) -> u1
(u2, target_picked_up) -> u3
(u2, else) -> u2
(u3, else) -> u3
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, has_door_key, u1) -> 0.1
(u1, door_open, u2) -> 0.2
(u1, key_lost, u1) -> -0.1
(u2, target_picked_up, u3) -> 1.0
feedback: The ordered core is sound: u0 -has_door_key-> u1 -door_open-> u2 respects the task order and the environment constraints (door_open cannot fire in u0 since it requires the key first; key_lost cannot fire in u0 and, while the door stays open, not in u2 either; a key drop after re-shutting the door in u2 is correctly absorbed by else since the obligation is already discharged). Persistent/event distinctions are handled correctly: re-rises of has_door_key in u1 and door_open remaining true in u2 fall to the per-state else self-loops, so no double rewards; key_lost is treated as a one-step event; every state has an else self-loop covering irrelevant or impossible propositions; reachability and all format headers including a nonempty FINAL_STATES are present. The rejection is on semantic fidelity of the accepting condition: FINAL_STATES declares u3, which is reachable only via (u2, target_picked_up) with reward 1.0, but the task 'if you take the key, you also have to open the door' never mentions the box. An agent that satisfies the task exactly, taking the key and then opening the door, ends in u2, which is not accepting, while the machine instead drives and pays its largest reward for the out-of-scope UnlockPickup box objective. u3 and its incoming transition are also extraneous for compactness, and the positive rewards sum to 1.3 with the dominant share on a task-irrelevant step, so the bounded progress-reward allocation is misaligned. The explicit -0.1 key_lost self-loop in u1 is acceptable and no state regression is needed, since taking the key irrevocably triggers the obligation. Direction only, not a rewrite: declare u2 as the sole final accepting state, remove u3 and (u2, target_picked_up) -> u3, and move the success reward onto the (u1, door_open, u2) transition so the terminal progress step carries the dominant bounded reward.

(u0, has_door_key) -> u1
(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, door_open) -> u2
(u1, key_lost) -> u1
(u1, else) -> u1
(u2, else) -> u2
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, has_door_key, u1) -> 0.1
(u1, key_lost, u1) -> -0.1
(u1, door_open, u2) -> 1.0
feedback: The RM correctly captures the task 'take the key, then open the door' as a minimal ordered chain u0 ->(has_door_key) u1 ->(door_open) u2, which matches the domain constraint that the door can only be opened after the matching key is carried. FINAL_STATES is present and nonempty (u2), declared in STATES, and accepting (task completion state). All three states are reachable and compact (3 states is minimal for two ordered milestones). Only propositions and 'else' appear in transitions. Irrelevant events (target_picked_up, re-firings of has_door_key in u1, door_open outside its slot) are absorbed by per-state else self-loops; door_open in u0 is unreachable by the domain constraint, and the else loop handles it safely regardless. The persistent/event distinction is handled correctly: key_lost is a one-step event, so the (u1, key_lost) self-loop applies the -0.1 penalty exactly once per drop, and since key_lost requires the door closed it can never fire after completion, so post-goal drops in u2 are unpunished. key_lost cannot fire in u0 because the RM leaves u0 on the very step has_door_key first holds. key_lost and door_open are mutually exclusive in u1 per the constraint table, so no ambiguous simultaneous events. Rewards are safe and bounded: 0.1 milestone plus 1.0 goal (max total 1.1), no reward farming (re-acquired has_door_key in u1 routes to else with no reward; u2 is a zero-reward absorbing state), and the -0.1 regression penalty on key_lost is explicit, bounded, and never punishes necessary behavior (toggling works with the key in hand, so dropping before opening is purely counterproductive). The order door_open-before-has_door_key is enforced structurally. Format follows the paper template exactly (REWARD_MACHINE/STATES/INITIAL_STATE/FINAL_STATES/TRANSITION_FUNCTION/REWARD_FUNCTION with (s,e)->s' and (s,e,s')->r syntax).

feedback: Accepted. The function set exactly matches the four environment-declared propositions (has_door_key, door_open, target_picked_up, key_lost) with no extras and no omissions; target_picked_up is unused by this RM but must be present, and it is. has_door_key, door_open, and target_picked_up reproduce the documented expressions verbatim: carrying check with type/color guard, grid scan with 'cell is not None' guards, mission-matched box via env.mission with no assumed color. key_lost implements the documented event semantics prev['has_door_key'] and not K and not D: it requires has_door_key true in the previous valuation, current key expression false, and current door_open expression false, so it fires only on the single drop step before the door opens and cannot co-occur with has_door_key, door_open, or target_picked_up. The extra guard on env.episode_memory['previous_valuation'] is harmless: at the first step the complete valuation has all propositions false (and if the snapshot were ever falsy the expression short-circuits to a falsy value, correctly yielding key_lost false). The snapshot is only read, never written; the functions mutate nothing, import nothing, call no actions, and are syntactically valid Python. Persistents read current state, the event compares current state against the read-only snapshot — all consistent with the environment's declared semantics.
